## Episode Thesis

Erik Strand, a fund manager at AUAG Fonder, argues that gold and silver have found new momentum since early August. He points to Japanese currency interventions, US Treasury Secretary Bessent's push to support the bond market and a Fed rate hike that failed to hurt metals, and expects quantitative easing to return within months, which he says would lift gold, silver and mining shares. He is also bullish on copper because demand from grid upgrades, AI data centres and defence is rising while little new supply is being found. The main risk he names is a bubble bursting among highly valued new AI and tech companies, which he thinks would cause only a short, sharp drop.
